title: Swap a hand blender's shaft for the whisk: both release buttons in, whisk clicked on
instruction: Take the blending shaft off the hand blender and lay it on the cork mat, then fit the whisk to the blender and let go of everything.
context: Hand (immersion) blenders are a common home kitchen appliance, and models such as Braun's MultiQuick 5 change between the blending shaft, the whisk and the chopper with a push-on fit: the shaft is released by pressing the two buttons on the sides of the motor part and drawn off, and an attachment is pushed on until it clicks (Braun manual). The swap is done in the middle of a recipe, with the blender unplugged first as the manual requires, and the used shaft is set down on a mat, not on the worktop. What goes wrong: with only one button in, the other latch keeps its hook, the shaft cocks and binds; pulling with no button in drags the whole blender across the counter; a whisk pushed on at a slant catches on one latch only and drops into the bowl at the first pulse.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A Braun MultiQuick 5 Vario hand blender (MQ5235 type), unplugged, lying on its back along y at x 300 mm. Motor part: white and grey plastic, 228 mm long (y +20 to +248 mm), 64 mm across (x) and 60 mm deep (z) with 10 mm chamfered edges, 0.62 kg (est). Its coupling end faces -y at y +20 mm: a square socket 41 mm across and 24 mm deep with a 5 mm lead-in. Two release buttons, black, 14 x 22 mm, one on each flank (facing +x and -x), centred 45 mm from the coupling end at mid-height, standing 3 mm proud; each travels 3 mm (flush) against a 2 N spring (est) and works a latch hook on the socket's opposite wall (a wedge, its tip 17.2 mm from the axis, 0.4 mm behind the lip of the attachment's stub): pressing a button moves its hook out toward that wall, and 1.8 mm or more draws it clear of the lip. (2) Blending shaft, 0.25 kg (est). Its plastic collar (56 mm across, 12 mm long) carries a stub 21 mm long on its face: a 33 mm wide core and a 38 mm square lip 5 mm long at the tip. The stub is in the socket to the stop (collar face on the coupling face, y +20 mm), both hooks behind the lip. Stainless stem 24 mm across to y -126 mm, then the bell, 60 mm across and 45 mm long (y -126 to -171 mm), resting on the table. (3) A wire whisk already clicked into its gearbox, 0.11 kg (est): gearbox a rounded-square housing 58 mm across its flats and 60 mm long (y -100 to -40 mm) with the same 21 mm stub on its top face (shoulder at y -40 mm, stub toward +y), the wire balloon 175 mm long (to y -275 mm) and 58 mm across at its widest; lying along y at x 200 mm. (4) A cork mat, 200 x 200 x 10 mm, fixed, centred at x 440 mm, y -170 mm (10 mm clear of the bell). With both buttons in, the stub slides out freely (about 0.3 N, est); with one hook still in, the lip catches on it and the shaft binds. Pushing a stub in, the lip rides up both hook ramps (about 2 N, est) and the hooks snap in behind it when the shoulder is within 0.4 mm of the coupling face. Nothing else is on the table. (5) Acceptance checks on the bought unit before the first trial (0-50 N spring scale, calipers): it measures 75 mm or less across the two buttons; squeezing both buttons flush across the body takes under 30 N; with both buttons in, the shaft draws off with under 5 N; with one button in, it stays on at 10 N; the whisk clicks on with under 15 N. A unit that fails a check is not used.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of all parts, the two buttons and both grippers. Shaft off: the shaft is not in the socket, wherever it lies. It counts as in the socket only while its stub's tip is more than 0.5 mm past the coupling face with its axis within 30 mm of the socket's and within 30 degrees of its direction; any other pose (on the mat, on the table, held up) is off. Shaft on mat: shaft off, its mid-point (along its 212 mm) within 100 mm of the mat's centre in x and in y, and its lowest point within 5 mm of the mat's top. Whisk home: the stub in the socket, the gearbox's shoulder face within 1 mm of the coupling face, its axis within 3 mm of the socket's and square within 3 degrees. Both hooks behind the lip: whisk home and both buttons within 0.4 mm of their rest height. Whisk on: home with both hooks behind the lip. Whisk seated: home but a button more than 0.4 mm in (a hook rides on the lip). Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from every part, and over that 1 s each part moves under 5 mm and turns under 5 degrees. Score 0 if at any time any part's lowest point is 30 mm below the table top (fallen off), and 0 unless hands off and the shaft is off. Otherwise: 1.0 shaft on the mat, whisk on; 0.5 whisk on with the shaft elsewhere (not on the mat), or the shaft on the mat and the whisk seated; 0.25 shaft off, otherwise; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: shaft off, look into the socket from the side and from above: no stub inside; shaft on mat, a 100 mm rule from the mat's centre to the shaft's mid-point (from above) and a 5 mm feeler under its lowest point; whisk home, a 1 mm feeler does not enter between gearbox and coupling face at the top, bottom or either side, and a protractor shows 3 degrees or less between the two axes; each hook separately, hold the motor part, press the +x button only and hold it in, pull the whisk straight out with a 10 N spring scale: it stays on (the -x hook holds it); release, press the -x button only and pull again: it stays on (the +x hook holds it); a whisk that comes off in either pull is seated, not on; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand and 30 fps video over the last 1 s with a 5 mm ruler and a 5 degree mark in view; fall, by eye. Do the pull tests last.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Model: each button is a sprung slider frame round the socket (2 N at 3 mm, est) carrying its latch hook on the opposite wall, a wedge (25 degree ramp, flat back face) that the stub's lip pushes aside and then stops; no software rule. Sizes, masses, springs and friction (0.35 plastic, 0.3 steel) are estimates to measure on a bought unit. The oval motor part is an octagon, the whisk wires solid hulls; the cord is not modelled (unplugged and taped down in a real trial).
reset_notes: Push the blending shaft onto the motor part until it clicks (collar face on the coupling face) and lay the blender on its back along y at x 300 mm, coupling end at y 20 mm. Press both buttons and draw the whisk off if it is on; lay the whisk at x 200 mm, gearbox toward +y, shoulder at y -40 mm. Tape the cord along the back. Nothing is consumed; between trials check that both hooks spring back and that the shaft binds with one button in.
